page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% via stress-ng. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations consistently register in the average range. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks (both read and write) is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, while the server handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds, its performance drops significantly for medium 7B models, with text generation speeds falling into the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and balanced memory allocation offer a reliable hardware profile for standard workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory or GPU-accelerated instances. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs will depend on external block storage. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, redis databases, text processing, and moderate multi-threaded application hosting.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, while multi-core operations, database tasks, and web serving throughput align with mid-range averages. This instance provides a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose applications, web servers, and redis operations.
